claim: Moving the whole world around the torus moves its future by the same amount.
derivation: The torus has no preferred place: every rule depends only on displacements between birds, beacons and obstacles (E1–E7).
So shifting everything by (7.25, −3.5), wrapped onto the torus, shifts the whole trajectory by that amount (E10).

The shift changes the rounding of positions by about 1e-15; over 30 steps that stays far below 1e-9 unless a bird sits within that distance of a neighbourhood boundary, which is vanishingly unlikely. Positions are compared the short way round.
Observables do not depend on where the flock is and agree to the same tolerance (E12–E14).
